lines.text: The result is wrong, and you have no idea how the agent got there.
Without a record, you guess. You rerun the task, tweak the prompt, and hope the problem goes away.
Agent R Q records every tool call and message, and keeps them in the task’s trajectory.
Open the task, and switch to the Trajectory tab. Everything the agent did is already there.
Each step sits in a lane, in order, with every tool call and every message.
Search the run for the step you suspect. Looking for edits, one search finds them all.
Click the entry, and you see exactly what the agent sent to the tool.
There it is. The agent edited the production file, when you expected the default config.
Now you know why. So you fix the instruction, and name the right file, instead of fixing a guess.
Rerun the task, and the agent edits the right file. The output is correct, and you can show why.
What is the strangest bug an agent ever created? Tell us in the comments, and try it at Agent R Q dot com.
